reasoning: Dates and the EO 12292 amendments check out, but the reason given for section 1-101 is contradicted by held sources. Section 1-101 makes payment of section 8(a)(2) additional compensation 'governed by the regulations contained in Executive Order No. 10000, as amended, which govern the payment of additional compensation in foreign areas (referred to as foreign post differential)'. The claim says EO 10000 'is itself still in the held record only as partially amended (EO 10261 revoked its section 404 and EO 10623 its sections 402 and 403)' and, in its member checks, that EO 10000 'remains in force as partially amended'. The held EO 10903 (January 9, 1961) section 5(a) revoked 'Parts I, III, IV, and V of Executive Order No. 10000'. Part I is 'Additional Compensation in Foreign Areas', the foreign post differential rules that section 1-101 points to. The same section also revoked EO 10261 and EO 10623 themselves. The claim's account of what survives of EO 10000, and so of what section 1-101 operates on, is wrong. The search for ends of the referenced regulations missed a held order.
